item.text: {"question_id":"2B.4","answer":"The supplied record does not establish that López Obrador personally adopted, resourced, and enforced lawful rules of engagement or prisoner safeguards in 2023. Government institutions cooperated with UN protection and accountability mechanisms, strengthened laws and training, and expanded refugee-system capacity, but the evidence does not show uniform enforcement or direct presidential command (BATCH-0015-E016; BATCH-0015-E018). Earlier commitments—the 2020 recognition of the UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances’ complaints competence and 2021 Kampala ratification—were positive institutional steps, but their 2023 remedial effects are not demonstrated; Amnesty instead assessed use-of-force safeguards as only partly implemented, arraigo as unrepealed, and independent investigation, accountability, and reparations as inadequate (BATCH-0051-E010). In 2023, Nuevo Laredo incidents involved soldiers allegedly shooting unarmed or wounded civilians and possibly staging a confrontation; the FGR-related account and forensic evidence remained contested, so these are serious allegations rather than final judicial findings (BATCH-0016-E005; BATCH-0010-E004). López Obrador publicly characterized the May incident as isolated, but the supplied evidence does not establish that he ordered or personally knew of the alleged conduct. His administration did maintain and expand military public-security deployment, while WOLA reported fewer armed confrontations and lower absolute levels of some serious violations than a decade earlier, alongside continuing excessive-force cases and weak accountability (BATCH-0047-E009). Overall, the evidence supports some institutional protection activity and mixed outcome evidence, but not demonstrated effective enforcement, prisoner safeguards, discipline, or remedy; attribution is strongest for the administration’s security framework and policy direction, not each alleged
